set_aside.subject: K-02 purity guarantee
set_aside.text: “no clock, no randomness” contradicts “it is no guarantee against code written to get around it”
set_aside.question: Is absence of clock and randomness an enforced property of every admitted and real function execution, or only a best-effort guard against ordinary standard-library access?
options: Every access path is prevented, so circumvention is a sandbox violation
Only designated entry points are blocked, and an implementation that circumvents them may be admitted and run
Circumvention may occur during execution but must be detected and make that execution fail
set_aside.default_guess: Treat clock and randomness as prohibited capabilities and fail any detected access as a sandbox violation.

witness.initial: A contract has a nonempty corpus, and an implementation obtains changing time or random data through a path not covered by the standard-library guard.
events: The kernel tries it over the corpus.
The kernel considers admission and activation.
outcomes: Under “no clock, no randomness” and the purity promise, the execution is refused as a sandbox violation and the implementation is not admitted.
Under “no guarantee against code written to get around it,” the trial may pass, the implementation may be admitted, and later runs may produce time- or chance-dependent outputs.
witness.observer: The agent sees a refusal versus admission, and flow users see deterministic versus varying outputs.

set_aside.subject: Clock and randomness interception boundary
set_aside.text: “the standard library's own entry points for them”
set_aside.question: Which Python operations are clock or randomness entry points that the sandbox withholds, including indirect and overlapping APIs?
options: Only the principal time and random modules
Every standard-library API that exposes wall time, monotonic time, entropy, random identifiers or seeded randomness
A declared allow/deny list identified by interpreter and standard-library version
set_aside.default_guess: Use an explicit versioned deny list covering every standard-library API that directly exposes time or entropy.

witness.initial: The sandbox permits only the Python standard library.
events: One agent submits a function using time.time().
Another submits one using datetime.now(), os.urandom(), secrets, uuid.uuid4(), or a monotonic/event-loop clock.
outcomes: An implementer reads all listed APIs as standard-library entry points for clock or randomness and withholds them.
Another implementer guards only time and random, allowing some or all of the indirect APIs.
witness.observer: Agents see different trial and admission results for the same function code across conforming kernels.

set_aside.subject: Observable result of withheld clock or randomness
set_aside.text: “The clock and randomness are withheld from a function that calls the standard library's own entry points for them”
set_aside.question: What observable result must a function execution produce when it calls a withheld entry point?
options: The execution fails with sandbox violation
The import or call raises a specified exception that function code may catch
The entry point returns a fixed deterministic value
The implementation is refused before execution
set_aside.default_guess: End the execution with a sandbox-violation failure that function code cannot catch.

witness.initial: An admitted candidate function calls time.time() during a trial case.
events: The agent asks the kernel to try the implementation.
outcomes: The trial ends with the action's named sandbox-violation failure.
The call instead raises a catchable exception or returns a fixed value, allowing the function to produce an ordinary successful output.
witness.observer: The agent sees failed trial evidence versus successful evidence and possible admission.

set_aside.subject: Deterministic admission and executions
set_aside.text: K-05 says “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus,” while K-02 says the guard “is no guarantee against code written to get around it”
set_aside.question: If code bypasses the guard and obtains time or randomness, what preserves the required deterministic admission verdict and the promise that trial and real executions are pure?
options: Such access must always be detected and refuse admission
Admission may be deterministic only for code that does not bypass the guard
The same implementation and corpus may receive different evidence or verdicts
set_aside.default_guess: Require bypass detection to turn the affected case into a sandbox violation and refuse admission.

witness.initial: A trial corpus contains an assertion whose result depends on a bypassed source of time or randomness.
events: The agent submits the same implementation against the unchanged corpus twice.
Each admission run observes a different clock or random value.
outcomes: K-05 requires the same deterministic verdict both times.
The new K-02 caveat permits one attempt to pass and another to fail if bypassed values affect the case.
witness.observer: The agent sees inconsistent admission and activation outcomes for identical immutable inputs.
